Any other bearer is refused before the body is read; then the actor must be an active superuser (go-api's PATCH /api/v1/admin/orgs/{org_id} is superuser only), checked on the live users row before anything is read for the request, and again inside the commit after the organization row lock.

rows.current_state_cache_behavior: No cache: a svc_authsess_ credential row is read live by token hash on every call; the organization's status and aggregate revision are read live, in one statement, on every call.
rows.disclosure_behavior: Every bearer refusal, for every credential class and reason, is the same 401 error.v1 invalid_credentials, and so is a go-api workload token with a well-formed body (the route is outside the workload per-operation set); a body that is not exactly one canonical organization_id is 400 malformed, a workload token's included (admit reads the body before the route refuses the workload); an organization that does not exist is 404 organization_not_found, named to any holder of the service credential; a store failure is 503 store_unavailable. The answer is the organization_id, its status and its revision read in one statement. The route writes nothing and no audit row.

primary_validator.description: servicecred.PG.CheckScope: the bearer must match svc_authsess_ + 43 base64url characters; its SHA-256 is looked up in public.internal_service_credentials and must be an unrevoked, unexpired auth-session-issuer row holding memberships:write (internal/auth/authapi/provisioning.go admit). A go-api workload token that passes admit is refused by the route itself (internal/auth/authapi/provisioning_state.go orgState): the route takes the session issuer service credential only. Any other bearer is refused before any read and before the body is read. The route reads no actor: it answers the status and revision of the organization named, for go-api's superuser PATCH of an organization's is_active.

rows.current_state_cache_behavior: No cache: on every exchange the Kubernetes subject is read from the Kubernetes TokenReview API and the workload registry rows, and the bootstrap subject from its credential_registry row with its workload and principal rows.
rows.disclosure_behavior: Every refusal after a valid request shape is the same 400 {"error":"invalid_grant"}; a malformed request is 400 {"error":"invalid_request"}; a TokenReview, signer or audit failure is 503 {"error":"temporarily_unavailable"} (a bootstrap registry read failure is the same 400 invalid_grant). No credential, claim or reason text is in any answer; the reason is only in the log line and the auth.workload.exchanges counter.

issued_credential.audience: the narrowed request audience: auth-service or dev-health-api, and one the workload is registered for
issued_credential.note: workload-token.v1 for the resolved workload principal; the lifetime is at most 300 s and never past the subject token's or the bootstrap credential's expiry; the jti is bound to the binding (Kubernetes) or the credential row (bootstrap) and the registry revision by the auth.workload.token_issued audit row.

primary_validator.description: handler.review: the Kubernetes TokenReview API authenticates the subject_token for the audience dev-health-workload-exchange; it is authenticated only by TokenReview: after a successful review its exp claim is read unverified, only to cap the issued token's lifetime, and it is never stored; the workload registry then resolves the reviewed ServiceAccount and narrows the audience and actions. With subject_token_type urn:dev-health:params:oauth:token-type:workload-bootstrap the request is the Compose bootstrap subject instead and never reaches TokenReview: handler.serveBootstrap (exchange_bootstrap.go:88) refuses a value outside the fcwlb_ shape before any store read, and workload.Store.ResolveBootstrap resolves the SHA-256 digest of the value (class, platform owner, workload kind, revocation, expiry, workload and principal state, and an audience both the workload and the credential hold).

rows.disclosure_behavior: An unknown, expired, used or wrong-purpose secret is the same 400; no detail names which.
rows.public_rationale: E-mail verification link secret in the token query parameter; single use, 24 hours, bound to the verification purpose, consumed on the database clock. Rate limited 10 per hour per client address and per e-mail query parameter value (normalized, unknown when absent); each distinct value has its own counter.

rows.disclosure_behavior: The same 202 body for a new address and a taken one; a taken address is told by mail and nothing about the requester is named.
rows.public_rationale: Creates an unverified local user from the body, and the organization with its owner membership unless the sign-up setting turns that off, then sends a verification link. Rate limited 3 per hour per client address.

rows.disclosure_behavior: The same 200 body for a known, unknown or already verified address; an unknown address runs a decoy that stores and sends nothing.
rows.public_rationale: Sends a verification link to the address in the body; the answer and the call sequence are the same for every address. Rate limited 3 per hour per client address and address.

rows.disclosure_behavior: The same 200 body for a known or unknown address; an unknown address runs a decoy that stores and sends nothing.
rows.public_rationale: Sends a reset link to the address in the body; the answer and the call sequence are the same for every address. Rate limited 3 per hour per client address and address.

rows.disclosure_behavior: An unknown, expired, used or wrong-purpose secret is the same 400; no detail names which.
rows.public_rationale: Password reset by link secret in the body; single use, 1 hour, bound to the reset purpose. The password is checked against the length bounds before the secret is consumed. Ends every session of the account.

rows.current_state_cache_behavior: No cache: the session row and the users row are read live on every request.
rows.disclosure_behavior: A wrong current password is a 403 with a fixed text; no field of the body is echoed, logged or audited.

issued_credential.note: go-api's access claims for the caller's new session, plus sid (hs256_compat class).
Under the eddsa access token class the access token of the caller's new session is the access-token.v1 JWS, signed by the active key of the key set; its signing kid is recorded on the new session.
The first opaque credential of the caller's new session, which starts a new family; every older session of the account is revoked.

primary_validator.description: authenticate: bearer HS256 access token with a sid claim; the session must be live and belong to sub, the users row active, and tv equal to users.token_version. The flow then requires the current password. An EdDSA user_access_token (JWT header alg EdDSA) is checked by the profile-routed validator with audience auth-service (scope auth:session): sid is required, and the session's token_version pin must equal users.token_version; the HS256 access token stays accepted (legacy_hs256 true).
